tool: go test -skip 'TestBuild$|TestPullNoBranchTags$' -coverprofile=cov.out ./... && go tool cover -func=cov.out | tail -1
notes: First run of this routine against captain - no prior ledger existed. Baseline 47.8% (204/427 statements), final 66.3% (283/427), a +18.5pp gain against the +15pp target. Both figures were measured with the exact same -skip flags for an apples-to-apples comparison. Environment blockers worked around: (1) the sandbox's docker daemon needed a manual start (`dockerd --iptables=false --storage-driver=vfs &`) since `service docker start` failed on an `ulimit: Operation not permitted` inside this container; (2) TestBuild and TestPullNoBranchTags are excluded from every `go test` invocation in this run (via -skip, not modified in the repo) because both call os.Exit() internally on failure, and both fail in this sandbox for reasons outside the code: TestBuild's fixture Dockerfiles (test/Simple, test/OneImage, test/noCaptainYML) all pull `golang:1.4.2`, whose schema-v1 manifest Docker Hub no longer serves ('manifest version 2, schema 1 has been removed'), and TestPullNoBranchTags pulls `alpine`, which this sandbox's registry access returns 403 Forbidden for. An os.Exit mid-test-binary is fatal to the whole `go test` process, silently zeroing out coverage for every other test, which is why they're excluded rather than left to fail normally. Four further pre-existing failures were left untouched (not fixed, not weakened, not skipped in-repo): TestColorCodes (fatih/color disables ANSI codes when stdout isn't a TTY, which it isn't under `go test`), and TestBuildImage/TestTagImage/TestImageExist (same golang:1.4.2 schema-v1 problem as above, but these three don't call os.Exit so they just fail their assertions instead of crashing the binary). None of these four are new or related to this run's changes. What was added, in order of impact: (1) cmd/captain (handleCmd, getNamespace) was previously 0% covered - the whole cobra CLI tree was untested - now 49.1% via a test that sets os.Args to ['captain','version'] and asserts the captured stdout, which exercises the entire command/flag-registration tree plus one real, harmless Run closure without touching docker or the network. (2) Build() went from 0% to 63.2% using a new test/scratch/Dockerfile (FROM scratch + a dummy COPY, so it builds instantly offline) covering: a fresh build, the 'already built this revision -> re-tag without rebuilding' skip path (asserted by checking the captured 'Building image' log line is absent), --force bypassing that skip, a user-supplied --tag, and a real dirty-working-tree state (via a temp untracked marker file) asserting revision/branch tagging is correctly suppressed while the plain 'latest' tag still lands. (3) pushImage/pullImage/removeImage (previously 0%, thin wrappers around docker.Client/exec but never called directly) now 100%, tested with deliberately-nonexistent image references so they fail fast without needing real registry access. (4) displaySyntaxError went 0% -> 100%: its only real caller (unmarshal) always feeds it YAML errors, against which its type assertion to *json.SyntaxError always fails, so its actual line/column formatting logic was dead code under existing tests; it's now exercised directly with a genuine *json.SyntaxError obtained from json.Unmarshal, which is the input type the function was written for. (5) isDirty() 0% -> 100% via a new test using a controlled temp untracked file (the existing TestGitIsDirty was left as its pre-existing no-op stub, per the 'never weaken existing tests' rule - a real assertion was added alongside it instead). (6) small gap-filling: configFile's empty-path default branch, GetApp's not-found branch. All new tests were run against a clean, committed working tree (git status verified empty) before this measurement, since several of them (isDirty, Build's dirty-repo branch) are directly sensitive to the repo's own git status.
next_target: Push and Pull are the largest remaining 0%-covered functions in captain.go (~29 and ~23 statements respectively). Both are structurally hard to test safely: every code path ends in a real `docker push`/`docker pull` network call, and any failure calls os.Exit() directly (same fatal-to-the-whole-binary problem worked around for TestBuild/TestPullNoBranchTags above) - there is no local/offline success path to exercise, unlike Build which could use a FROM-scratch fixture. Testing them for real would need either a refactor introducing an injectable command runner (a production-code seam, which this routine prefers to avoid) or accepting that any real assertion first requires registry credentials this sandbox doesn't have. Second-largest: the Run closures for cmdBuild/cmdTest/cmdPush/cmdPull/cmdPurge/cmdSelfUpdate inside handleCmd are still unexercised (only cmdVersion's is, via TestHandleCmdVersion) - each would need to actually invoke Build/Test/Push/Pull/Purge/SelfUpdate through the CLI, hitting the same docker/network wall. Build()'s 'no local git repository found' branch (~10 statements) is genuinely dead under any test run inside a git clone, since isGit() is always true there; only reachable with a seam to fake isGit(), not pursued here. SelfUpdate/downloadFile/findLastVersion's remaining gaps are their network-failure branches, which would need a fault-injectable HTTP client.
